stories.headline: Bank of Canada expected to hold rates as inflation cools
stories.dek: Economists see no change on Wednesday after September prices rose less than forecast.
stories.whatHappened: Most economists polled this week expect the Bank of Canada to keep its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday. September's consumer price index rose 1.9% from a year earlier, a little below forecasts, while the jobless rate held near 7%.
stories.whyItMatters: The rate sets what Canadians pay on variable mortgages and lines of credit. A hold would mean no relief for borrowers this month, but signals the bank thinks inflation is back under control.
stories.explainSimply: Think of the central bank as a thermostat for the economy. Prices have stopped heating up, so it is likely to leave the dial where it is for now.
stories.background:
The bank cut its rate several times over the past two years as inflation eased from its 2022 peak.

It meets eight times a year and publishes a full economic outlook with four of those decisions, including this one.

keyTerms.definition: The interest rate the central bank sets, which other lending rates follow.

stories.headline: British Columbia closes its wildfire season early
stories.dek: Autumn rain ended a season that burned less land than the last three.
stories.whatHappened: The BC Wildfire Service said on Monday that the province's fire season is over after a week of heavy rain on the coast and the interior. About 400,000 hectares burned this year, well below the record set in 2023.
stories.whyItMatters: A quieter year gives crews and towns time to rebuild firebreaks and clear dry brush before next summer. It also eases pressure on insurance costs in fire-prone areas.
stories.explainSimply: After several summers of huge fires, this one was more like a normal year, and the rain has now put out what was left.
stories.background:
British Columbia has had some of the worst fire seasons on record in recent years, with whole towns evacuated.

The province has since added crews and paid for more brush clearing near communities.

keyTerms.definition: A strip of land cleared of fuel to stop a fire spreading.

whatToWatch: Next spring's snowpack and drought forecasts

also.headline: Toronto's Finch West light rail line carries its first riders
also.whatHappened: The long-delayed Finch West light rail line opened to the public on Sunday, adding 18 stops across the city's north end.
also.whyItMatters: It cuts travel times for neighbourhoods that have relied on crowded buses.

also.headline: Housing starts slowed in September, the national housing agency says
also.whatHappened: Builders began work on fewer homes in September than in August, mostly because of a drop in new condo projects in Toronto and Vancouver.

also.headline: Maple Leafs win their home opener in overtime
also.whatHappened: Toronto beat Montreal 3–2 in overtime on Saturday night in front of a sold-out crowd.

also.headline: Quebec reaches a tentative deal with its largest teachers' union
also.whatHappened: The Quebec government and the province's largest teachers' union reached a tentative agreement on pay and class sizes, ending talks that began in the spring.
also.whyItMatters: Members still need to vote on it in the coming weeks.

also.headline: A Canadian documentary wins the audience award at the Vancouver film festival
also.whatHappened: A documentary about a Nunavut youth choir won the audience award at the Vancouver International Film Festival.
